citation: Liu et al. (2025), The Korean Journal of Pain
title: Knowledge, mechanisms, and intervention of the polytrauma clinical triad in military pain medicine
authors: Qinghua Liu; Peipei Qiu; Tao Ma; Yali Zhao; Shihui Fu; Minglong Gao; Zeguo Feng; Long Feng
pain_condition_detail: polytrauma clinical triad (chronic pain, PTSD, TBI) in military personnel; includes musculoskeletal pain, back/neck pain, headache/migraine, neuropathic pain
context_note: US military population; active duty service members and veterans of Iraq/Afghanistan conflicts
bps_function_set: conclusion; intervention rationale; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses 'biopsychosocial approach' as a rhetorical recommendation for interdisciplinary care in the abstract and conclusion, but never defines the model, operationalizes it, or applies it to any analysis. The review is organized by disease (pain, PTSD, TBI) rather than by biopsychosocial domains.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper asserts bidirectional relationships between pain and sleep, and directional effects of stress on neural remodeling affecting cognition. TBI is said to impair perceptual functions leading to pain. However, no integrated three-domain pathway is specified; biological, psychological, and social factors are mostly listed in parallel.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper asserts PCT components are interrelated but does not specify a unified mechanism, each disease is discussed separately with separate mechanisms
conceptual_tensions_2: Biopsychosocial approach is recommended but never defined or applied, the review is organized by disease rather than by biopsychosocial domains
conceptual_tensions_3: Social factors are mentioned only as risk factors or outcomes, not integrated into the mechanistic account of PCT
additional_observations_1: The paper is a narrative review of the polytrauma clinical triad (chronic pain, PTSD, TBI) in military populations, not a systematic review of the biopsychosocial model
additional_observations_2: Biological content is elaborated with detailed mechanisms (sensitization, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, brain imaging), while psychological content is limited to named conditions (depression, anxiety) without construct definitions
additional_observations_3: The review uses the term 'biopsychosocial approach' only twice (abstract and conclusion) as a rhetorical recommendation for interdisciplinary care, with no analytic follow-through
synthesis_note: This narrative review on the polytrauma clinical triad in military populations uses 'biopsychosocial approach' as a concluding recommendation but never defines or operationalizes the model. Biological mechanisms are elaborated, psychological constructs are named but undefined, and social factors are minimal. No three-domain integration is achieved; the review is organized by disease rather than by biopsychosocial domains.
coding_rationale: Typology is pseudo_bps because BPS label appears but social domain is minimal and no integration is achieved. Triadic integration is partial because bio-psych and bio-social links are directional/mentioned but no three-domain pathway exists. Bio-dominant due to extensive biological mechanism coverage.

citation: Liu et al. (2025), The Korean Journal of Pain
title: Knowledge, mechanisms, and intervention of the polytrauma clinical triad in military pain medicine
authors: Qinghua Liu; Peipei Qiu; Tao Ma; Yali Zhao; Shihui Fu; Minglong Gao; Zeguo Feng; Long Feng
pain_condition_detail: Post-traumatic chronic pain, post-traumatic stress disorder, and traumatic brain injury in active-duty service members and veterans.
context_note: Military active-duty service members and veterans, mainly U.S. Iraq/Afghanistan veterans; care includes military health system, Veterans Health Administration, and Multi-trauma Care System.
bps_function_set: conclusion; intervention rationale; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The BPS label is not operationalized as variables; the paper uses PCT to organize chronic pain, PTSD, and TBI, then discusses mechanisms and treatments. BPS appears mainly to justify interdisciplinary, multimodal care.
integration_mechanism_summary: No fully triadic mechanism. The paper proposes bio-psych mechanisms such as chronic stress neuroendocrine/immune/metabolic mediators affecting cognition/mood, brain injury/disorganized pain modulation, and pain-sleep aggravation; social factors are mostly consequences or care-system contexts.
conceptual_tensions_1: Although each disease of this triad could occur in isolation, it is valuable to know whether a single condition increases the risk of the entire triad and whether the rest of PCT needs to be screened for
conceptual_tensions_2: the survival rate of wounded soldiers has exceeded 90%, but the treatment rate for pain is not as high as the survival rate [ - ]
conceptual_tensions_3: opioids are the most efficacious agents for acute and chronic pain associated with neurological or tissue injury [ ]
conceptual_tensions_4: Opioids are not currently recommended as the first treatment for any type of chronic pain in clinical practice, and even many guidelines do not recommend their use in specific populations such as younger groups with non-cancerous pain [ ]
conceptual_tensions_5: Because neurobiological mechanisms of PTSD are not well established, available pharmacological treatment options are currently limited
additional_observations_1: PCT, not a formal BPS model, is the paper's main organizing unit
additional_observations_2: Social content is mostly about work, family burden, VHA/military health systems, and costs rather than social determinants of pain
additional_observations_3: The BPS label appears only in the abstract and conclusion
additional_observations_4: The paper's strongest integration is between pain, PTSD/TBI, sleep, cognition, and suicide risk
additional_observations_5: Interventions span opioids, psychotherapy, rehabilitation, complementary medicine, and shared decision-making
additional_observations_6: Sleep is treated both as a clinical complication and as a lifestyle/treatment target
synthesis_note: This review treats PCT as chronic pain plus PTSD plus TBI, with biological mechanisms and psychological symptoms developed, social effects as consequences and system burdens. The BPS label is used in the abstract and conclusion to support interdisciplinary, multimodal care, not as an operational framework.
coding_rationale: BPS label is an intervention rationale; bio and psych are elaborated, social is mentioned. Bio-psych mechanisms exist; triadic integration is partial because social factors remain consequences/context.

title: Knowledge, mechanisms, and intervention of the polytrauma clinical triad in military pain medicine
authors: Qinghua Liu; Peipei Qiu; Tao Ma; Yali Zhao; Shihui Fu; Minglong Gao; Zeguo Feng; Long Feng
pain_condition_detail: polytrauma clinical triad (chronic pain, PTSD, TBI) in military personnel
context_note: Military combat and deployment context, US and allied forces
bps_function_set: background framing; intervention rationale; organizing principle
bps_operationalization_summary: Organizes content around three interrelated conditions (pain, PTSD, TBI) without defining BPS model itself; uses BPS label to justify interdisciplinary treatment but does not operationalize the three-domain integration
integration_mechanism_summary: No three-domain integration proposed. Some pairwise relationships noted: PTSD worsens pain, pain and sleep disturbance are bidirectional, TBI associated with chronic pain development. No mechanistic pathways specified.
conceptual_tensions_1: BPS label used to justify multimodal treatment without substantive three-domain integration
conceptual_tensions_2: Biological mechanisms (central sensitization, neuroinflammation) mentioned but not linked to psychological/social factors
conceptual_tensions_3: PTSD and TBI treated as psychological/neurological conditions rather than integrated with pain through BPS framework
additional_observations_1: Focuses on military population with combat-related injuries rather than general chronic pain population
additional_observations_2: Treatment section emphasizes multimodal pharmacological and non-pharmacological approaches without BPS integration
additional_observations_3: No formal definition of biopsychosocial model provided despite using the label
additional_observations_4: High prevalence data (up to 42.1%) for PCT in military population
synthesis_note: This review organizes content around three interrelated conditions (chronic pain, PTSD, TBI) in military population using BPS label to justify multimodal treatment. Psychological domain is elaborated with PTSD, cognitive impairment, and sleep disturbance. Biological domain is mentioned with central sensitization, nerve injury, and neuroinflammation. Social domain is minimal, focusing on family burden and medical expenses. No three-domain integration proposed; some pairwise relationships noted. BPS used as organizing principle and treatment justification without substantive integration.
coding_rationale: Psychological domain elaborated with multiple constructs; biological mentioned but not integrated; social minimal. BPS label used for treatment justification without defining model or integrating domains. Triadic integration absent.
